name: Garrison
label: Revelation
lede: Joe Grillo and Ed McNamara wrote songs in Boston for a year before their first show, then played hundreds more across the US, Europe and Japan, trying to make Drive Like Jehu sound like a pop band.

eras.title: A year in a practice room before anyone heard them
eras.text: Joe Grillo and Ed McNamara grew up together in Shrewsbury, outside Worcester. McNamara had fronted the math-emo band Iris and run an all-ages room called The Space; Grillo had played in Stricken for Catherine in New Hampshire. In Boston they wanted something stripped-down and heavy.

years.big: "There's the music I didn't know I always wanted to make"
years.h: Joe Grillo and Ed McNamara write for a year with no show booked
years.p: Grillo moves to Boston and McNamara follows, with drummer Guy D'Annolfo in early. Grillo was talking to Lollipop in 1999 about hearing Bitch Magnet.
years.xp:
The band practiced at 3 Wadsworth Street in Allston. McNamara came with a track record: for more than five years, in three incarnations, he ran The Space, an all-ages warehouse in Worcester that hosted Metroschifter, June of 44 and Thurston Moore.

Asked by Lollipop about influences, McNamara listed Bitch Magnet, Slint, Rodan, Don Caballero and Drive Like Jehu as the records he found in the early '90s.

years.h: Garrison debut on June 29, a day after Stricken for Catherine's last show
years.p: Bassist Andy White completes the lineup. Joe Grillo goes from his old band's farewell on June 28 to a new band's first night.

years.h: Boston's Espo Records puts out Garrison's first record, a 7" called 24
years.p: Early demo material, pressed in the same year as the band's first show.

eras.title: Songs, not math
eras.text: Revelation signed Garrison while Boston's heavy scene was blowing up around Converge and Cave In. The band recorded with Kurt Ballou and Brian McTernan, toured constantly, and kept saying they were writing songs, not puzzles.

q: We consciously try to write songs
years.h: Revelation puts out The Bend Before the Break, 200 copies on green vinyl
years.p: REV 83 is Garrison's debut for the label, recorded at Fort Apache studio with Brian McTernan.
years.xp:
McNamara told Lollipop that year the band consciously tried to write songs: honest lyrics inside arrangements that hold your attention, rather than technical showing off. He and Grillo name-checked The Cure, Pixies, Operation Ivy, Slint and [[Don Caballero|b93697af-a318-417a-b16e-a9eb47fbe2f8]].

Booking was a home job. Grillo said they were talking to someone, but "he's not a 'booking agent' like the ones you usually think of."

yt: "After the Fight" at the PAC in Attleboro, Massachusetts, 2000
years.h: A Mile in Cold Water is Garrison's first full-length, REV 93
years.p: Recorded in Boston. The first vinyl pressing was 220 copies on opaque blue.
years.xp: Iodine Recordings later remastered it, with Ballou mixing from the original tape and new artwork by Dan McCarthy.

yt: Serious Heavy Drama, cut from 2000 tour footage
years.h: A van tour with Elliott and Boy Sets Fire, filmed by the band itself
years.p: Garrison spend 2000 on the road with [[Elliott|b3250fd8-d202-4d4a-8fb3-1fdf88176aff]] and [[Boy Sets Fire|ba561cc7-2050-47d3-8bc2-c645a1393d90]]. The footage sits in a box until Iodine uses it for the Serious Heavy Drama video in 2021.
years.xp:
Duncan Wilder Johnson edited it, and it premiered with New Noise Magazine on November 10, 2021. Grillo said he was glad the tapes turned up because they captured "traveling the country in a van with friends."

He also said the song's title was a tongue-in-cheek reference to the emo scene at the time. It was the band's regular opener.

years.h: Garrison and Hundred Reasons swap sides on a split EP
years.p: Simba Recordings releases it in the UK and Iodine in the US.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia · Revelation Records
years.h: Be a Criminal is the second and last Garrison album for Revelation
years.p: REV 103. The vinyl ran 307 copies on grey and white marble and 1,757 on black.
years.xp: Perfect Sound Forever credits J. Robbins as the producer of Be a Criminal.

years.h: Guy D'Annolfo and Andy White step out of Garrison
years.p: Joe Grillo and Ed McNamara carry on with a changing cast, including Jason Carlin, Matt LaVonture and Ethan Dussault.

eras.title: The EPs, then the end
eras.text: Garrison kept releasing and kept touring, as far as Europe and Japan, before calling it. Sources disagree on the exact show count, but it runs into the hundreds.

years.h: Two EPs and a split with Orange Island close out the catalog
years.p: The Model and The Silhouette come out in 2003, along with the Orange Island split on Iodine.

years.h: Garrison end it, and the members split into other bands
years.p: McNamara joins Campaign for Real Time; Grillo joins [[Gay for Johnny Depp|8fab478a-6800-4b5c-ae98-01d65eeec146]].
years.xp: The accounts of the run differ. Perfect Sound Forever says the band played close to 400 shows in the US, Europe and Japan and broke up in early 2004. Wikipedia counts 353 shows and dates the end to 2003.

eras.title: The vault, then the stage
eras.text: Arctic Rodeo and Iodine went back through the catalog: rarities, a first vinyl LP of The Bend Before the Break, and A Mile in Cold Water back on LP. The reissues got the original four in a room again.

years.h: Arctic Rodeo digs up the b-sides for TV or the Atom Bomb
years.p: The German label gathers the singles, b-sides and rarities from across Garrison's career.

years.h: The Bend Before the Break finally gets a full LP
years.p: Iodine Recordings adds unreleased tracks from 1998 to 2004 and new artwork by Dan McCarthy.

years.cap: Flyer for the Middle East Downstairs reunion show, Cambridge, October 6, 2023
years.h: The original four reunite for three shows
years.p: With A Mile in Cold Water back on LP, Joe Grillo, Ed McNamara, Guy D'Annolfo and Andy White play the Middle East Downstairs in Cambridge, Ralph's Chadwick Diner in Worcester, and The Wooly in Gainesville during The Fest.
